fields.ander882\n\n 2012-05-30 17:01\n\ndevelop:
ok, I found the problem.
All of the format information for fonts, etc is written to file BEFORE the begin_report procedure is called in the reports. begin_report is also where the report is made, the scale factor is known, and the fonts are scaled properly. So in short, the default font info is written to file, then calculated correctly.

To fix this error, move everything in the begin_report section to init (because the scaling of the fonts is the last thing done in begin_report) and BAM! works great.

two ways to fix:

Simply move everything in begin_report to init. No real problem with this.
Update the document generator to run begin_report FIRST, then start making the actual file (.odt, .pdf, etc), then run write_report.

2) technically makes more sense as write_report should ONLY do what it says. write the report. init should only do basic setup and begin_report... Well it is somewhere in the middle but it should NOT start writing anything.

2) could also introduce errors in other reports which is a BIG problem

Is there any specification written as to WHAT init, begin_report, write_report should do and the general flow control (overview) of what happens before, in between, and after these procedures?

Craig A.

fields.paulfranklin\n\n 2012-05-31 13:16\n\ndev:
Yes, as you've discovered, only three (official) reports
say "def begin_report" and two of them are yours. And while
"begin_report" is called as part of the normal report
generation (CLI, GUI, and book report), the normal one which
is thus hit (for everybody but the three of you) is just a
"pass" -- so I guess it depends on what you want to accomplish
in your two reports, where you then put the code to accomplish it.

I will, however, point out that this is a bug against 3.4.x
and so I don't think rewriting the report system is the right
way to fix it. Anything major like that should only be done
in trunk, and probably only after much discussion.

Thanks.

I applied your patch and made a five-generation descendant
chart and indeed all the text was shrunken, so as far as I'm
concerned you can apply the patch to gramps34 (and trunk)
and mark this bug as resolved.

I don't use ODT except when testing (as now) and so I was
a little surprised to see that the text in the boxes wasn't
what I was expecting. I had two (at most) lines per box
and the top line was centered in the box while the second
line was then left-justified against the edge of the top
string (not the box). An interesting combination. But I
don't care and at any rate that is certainly not what this
bug is about.

Thank you for fixing this. Now I can use both output types
when I make my book reports (and use your reports), whereas
before I had to use only PDF. So now I can compare the two.
